question: What skin changes usually show up in long-term onchocerciasis?

options.A: Bright red circular rashes
options.B: Widespread skin bruising
options.C: Severe itching and skin thickening
options.D: Painful pus-filled blisters

explanation: Chronic infections cause intense itching. Over time, all that scratching leads to thickened skin with a texture people sometimes compare to lizard skin.

question: Why does scarring often develop inside the fallopian tubes after an infection?

options.A: Excess hormones thicken the muscular walls
options.B: Blood clots block the internal blood vessels
options.C: Calcium deposits harden the ciliated lining
options.D: Healing tissue creates fibrous adhesions

explanation: Just like a skin wound forms a scar as it heals, inflamed tubal tissue can form fibrous bands that narrow or block the tube.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the traditional 'essential cleans' during delivery?

options.A: Clean surface for the mother
options.B: Clean cord cutting instruments
options.C: Clean surgical gloves for all family members
options.D: Clean hands of the birth attendant

explanation: Family members cheering mum on don't need surgical gloves! The essential cleans focus on the birth attendant's hands, the perineum, the surface, and cord care.

question: What is the job of the jelly-like substance (colloid) found inside your thyroid gland?

options.A: To provide a rigid structural framework supporting the larynx
options.B: To manufacture parathyroid hormone for the posterior glands
options.C: To store thyroid hormone precursors until they are ready for release
options.D: To produce calcitonin for the regulation of blood calcium levels

explanation: Colloid acts like a storage warehouse inside the thyroid follicles, holding onto hormone building blocks safely until your body gives the signal to release them.

question: Why does the baby's head need to twist (internal rotation) as it travels down the birth canal?

options.A: To stimulate the onset of maternal pushing reflexes
options.B: To ensure the placenta detaches from the uterine wall
options.C: To adapt to the changing shape and wider dimensions of the pelvic outlet
options.D: To prevent early rupture of the amniotic membranes

explanation: The pelvis changes shape from top to bottom, so the baby has to twist slightly to fit through the widest parts easily.

question: Why do many patients delay seeking medical help for faecal incontinence?

options.A: Doctors rarely ask about bowel habits
options.B: Feelings of shame and social stigma
options.C: The condition always resolves on its own
options.D: Lack of any physical discomfort

explanation: Social embarrassment and stigma often cause individuals to hide their symptoms, preventing them from receiving timely medical evaluation and support. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h1)

question: A patient asks why she noticed cervical changes after starting a new oral contraceptive pill. What is the best way to explain it?

options.A: The pill permanently scars the muscular walls of the uterus.
options.B: The pill causes the outer cervical skin to become very dry and crack open.
options.C: The hormone estrogen in the pill causes inner cervical cells to shift outward.
options.D: The pill creates a bacterial infection that eats away at the outer cervix.

explanation: Birth control pills contain estrogen, which signals the inner cervical cells to expand outward. Explaining this simply to your patients helps ease their worries completely!

question: Why do many community farming systems encourage seed saving?

options.A: To ensure that all seeds are patented by international corporations
options.B: To preserve climate-resilient seed varieties instead of buying commercial hybrids
options.C: To increase the overall cost of planting basic vegetables
options.D: To prevent any crops from growing during the dry season

explanation: You got it! Saving seeds helps farmers keep traditional, hardy crops growing locally without always having to buy expensive commercial seeds.

question: Why do some patients pressure doctors to write unnecessary prescriptions?

options.A: They believe getting a drug means they received good care
options.B: They are legally required to buy three drugs per visit
options.C: They prefer paying more money for hospital visits
options.D: They want to study pharmacology at the university

explanation: Many patients feel unsatisfied with a consultation unless they walk away with physical items like tablets or syrups. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which skin layer acts as the main rate-limiting barrier to drug absorption?

options.A: Dermal blood vessels
options.B: Hypodermal tissue
options.C: Stratum corneum
options.D: Subcutaneous fat

explanation: The stratum corneum, found in the outermost epidermis layer, consists of tough dead cells that heavily restrict foreign substances and drugs from entering. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h2)

question: Why should you do a quick physical assessment right after the steam session ends?

options.A: To check if the bed linens need washing
options.B: To evaluate how well the treatment worked
options.C: To see if the patient needs a snack or drink
options.D: To make sure the electrical cord is cool

explanation: Spot on! Comparing your notes now with your baseline check tells you if the therapy did its job.

question: During a vaginal examination, a midwife notices the baby's skull bones are overlapping tightly and cannot be pushed apart with a finger. How is this graded?

options.A: Grade 1 moulding
options.B: Grade 2 moulding
options.C: Grade 0 moulding
options.D: Grade 3 moulding

explanation: When the bones overlap strongly and won't budge under finger pressure, we call that Grade 3 moulding. It's an important sign that tells us to watch out for tight squeezes (cephalopelvic disproportion)!

question: How is custodial care traditionally provided in most Nigerian communities?

options.A: Exclusively through government-funded nursing homes
options.B: By international insurance companies paying for home aides
options.C: Through mandatory hospital stays for all elderly citizens
options.D: Through extended family networks and shared family duty

explanation: Nigerian culture traditionally relies on the extended family system to care for aging or disabled relatives at home. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h6)

question: What is the main difference between quarantine and isolation?

options.A: Quarantine restricts people who were exposed but are not yet sick, while isolation separates those who are already confirmed sick.
options.B: Quarantine involves giving preventive medications, while isolation involves performing major surgical procedures.
options.C: Quarantine is only used for waterborne diseases, whereas isolation is reserved exclusively for vector-borne illnesses.
options.D: Quarantine takes place in private homes, while isolation can only happen in national research laboratories.

explanation: Easy way to remember: Isolation is for those who are already sick, while quarantine is for those who were exposed and are waiting to see if they fall ill.

question: Why is it so important to separate general rubbish from hazardous waste right when you throw it away?

options.A: To reduce the overall weight of general waste bins
options.B: To make it easier for administrative staff to empty trash cans
options.C: To prevent clean items from becoming dangerous and costly to treat
options.D: To comply with building design codes for hospitals

explanation: You got it! If you mix regular trash with infectious waste, the whole batch becomes contaminated. That drives up the volume—and the cost—of special waste disposal drastically.

question: Which of these details is NOT necessary to write down in your notes after a blood transfusion?

options.A: The name of the blood donor's family members
options.B: The product serial number and volume given
options.C: The start and stop times of the infusion
options.D: The patient's post-transfusion vital signs

explanation: Donor privacy is key! Blood banks keep donor details strictly confidential, so they never appear in your patient's chart.

question: Which genetic combination is most commonly found in biological males?

options.A: One Y chromosome only
options.B: Two X chromosomes
options.C: One X and one Y chromosome
options.D: Three X chromosomes

explanation: Great job! Biological males usually inherit an X chromosome from the mother and a Y chromosome from the father, giving an XY pairing.

question: What type of hearing loss does a buildup of earwax (cerumen) usually cause?

options.A: Permanent nerve damage
options.B: Sensorineural hearing loss
options.C: Central auditory processing disorder
options.D: Conductive hearing loss

explanation: Earwax blocks sound waves from traveling down the ear canal. This stops sound conduction without hurting the inner ear nerves!

question: How does school-based health education impact the wider community?

options.A: Parents lose responsibility for teaching their children
options.B: Communities stop building local health clinics entirely
options.C: Local hospitals experience a permanent drop in staffing
options.D: Children take healthy habits home to their families

explanation: Students act as health messengers, sharing hygiene and nutrition practices learned at school with their families at home. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h6)

question: A nurse is getting ready to give activated charcoal to a patient who swallowed poison. Which of these actions is a dangerous mistake?

options.A: Administering the charcoal through an intravenous infusion line
options.B: Confirming the time of the poison ingestion with family
options.C: Ensuring a suction machine is ready at the bedside
options.D: Checking the patient's airway before giving the liquid

explanation: Yikes! Activated charcoal belongs strictly in the stomach via the mouth or tube. Giving it into a vein (IV) is fatal. Always double-check your routes!

question: Why do nurses always warn patients with bleeding problems to stay away from everyday painkillers like ibuprofen?

options.A: NSAIDs increase blood pressure to dangerous levels and trigger acute strokes
options.B: NSAIDs instantly destroy all stored vitamin K reserves located inside the liver
options.C: NSAIDs negatively interfere with normal platelet aggregation and increase bleeding risks
options.D: NSAIDs cause the kidneys to stop producing red blood cells permanently

explanation: Medications like ibuprofen and aspirin get in the way of platelets sticking together, making it much harder for your body to stop any bleeding.

question: A new mum just had a repair for a fourth-degree tear and is terrified of her first toilet trip. What should be in her care plan?

options.A: Providing daily enemas to clear the lower bowel completely
options.B: Instructing her to restrict all oral fluid intake until she passes stool
options.C: Applying strong pressure dressings over the anus to prevent stool passage
options.D: Administering prescribed stool softeners and encouraging high-fiber foods

explanation: Soft stools mean she won't have to strain, which keeps the delicate stitches in her anal area safe and undisturbed.

question: What should a nurse do when a woman in labor develops a complication too severe for a primary health clinic?

options.A: Quickly arrange a safe transfer to a higher-level facility with CEmONC
options.B: Wait until morning to see if she gets better
options.C: Try to perform surgery right there without proper tools
options.D: Tell the family to take her home for local herbs

explanation: Brilliant! Prompt referral saves lives when your clinic lacks the surgery and blood transfusion resources needed for severe emergencies.

question: What does the SBAR acronym stand for during a patient handover?

options.A: Symptoms, Breathing, Activity, Recovery
options.B: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.C: Safety, Blood, Airway, Respiration
options.D: Staff, Beds, Ambulances, Reports

explanation: Easy peasy! SBAR stands for Situation, Background, Assessment, and Recommendation. It keeps your shift handovers clear and professional.

question: What are the two primary functions of the ovaries during this monthly cycle?

options.A: Maturing follicles and producing sex hormones
options.B: Digesting fats and making red blood cells
options.C: Producing urine and filtering blood cells
options.D: Storing waste and regulating body temperature

explanation: The ovaries have a dual role of developing the female gametes inside follicles and secreting vital hormones like estrogen and progesterone. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h1)

question: What sign tells you a patient is struggling and working extra hard to breathe?

options.A: Warm and dry skin on the forehead
options.B: Use of accessory neck and chest muscles
options.C: Symmetrical and slow chest wall rise
options.D: Quiet and relaxed abdominal movement

explanation: When breathing gets tough, the neck and shoulder muscles kick in to help pull air in. Watch those shoulders!

question: If you check the blood pressure of a patient with Addison's disease, what are you most likely to find?

options.A: Normal blood pressure
options.B: Low blood pressure
options.C: High blood pressure
options.D: Fluctuating high pressure

explanation: Without enough aldosterone, the body loses too much salt and water. Less fluid in the pipes means low blood pressure (hypotension). Makes complete sense when you trace the plumbing!

question: Why does blood mostly bypass a baby's lungs before birth?

options.A: The lungs are filled with fluid and not yet used for breathing
options.B: The lungs are too small to hold any blood at all
options.C: Blood cannot reach the upper chest before birth
options.D: Oxygen is produced directly inside the lung tissue

explanation: Great thinking! Foetal lungs are full of amniotic fluid and don't do breathing work yet, so the body routes most of the blood around them. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h1)

question: Which health problem is a woman more likely to face later in life if she had preeclampsia during pregnancy?

options.A: Higher lifetime risk of heart disease
options.B: Chronic chest allergies
options.C: Permanent blindness in both eyes
options.D: Getting chronic kidney stones

explanation: Having preeclampsia is like a stress test for the body's blood vessels, meaning these women have a higher chance of heart and blood pressure issues later in life.

question: What classic set of signs points to cardiac tamponade?

options.A: Slow pulse, flushed skin, and high temperature
options.B: High BP, strong pulses, and clear breath sounds
options.C: Fast breathing, pinpoint pupils, and quiet tummy
options.D: Low BP, muffled heart sounds, and swollen neck veins

explanation: Known as Beck's triad, these three signs (low blood pressure, muffled heart tones from fluid, and distended neck veins) are huge red flags for tamponade! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h7)

question: Which type of cardiomyopathy involves abnormal thickening of the heart muscle walls?

options.A: Ischemic cardiomyopathy
options.B: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
options.C: Restrictive cardiomyopathy
options.D: Dilated cardiomyopathy

explanation: 'Hyper-' means over or excessive, and 'trophic' relates to growth. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy means the heart muscle has grown too thick!

question: As a nurse, what is a key duty when taking a patient's medication history?

options.A: Prescribing new antibiotics if the patient feels weak
options.B: Asking specifically about self-prescribed drugs, herbs, and leftover pills
options.C: Telling the patient to stop asking questions about their treatment
options.D: Selling safe over-the-counter drugs directly from the nursing station

explanation: That's right! Always dig deeper during assessments to find out what informal remedies or leftover pills the patient has taken.

question: Why is it helpful for nurses to know a hormone's chemical structure?

options.A: It shows whether the hormone is made of white blood cells
options.B: It predicts how they travel in blood and interact with target cells
options.C: It dictates the exact caloric value of the hormone in the diet
options.D: It determines the exact time of day the gland will secrete them

explanation: Knowing whether a hormone is water-soluble or fat-soluble helps us understand how it moves through the blood and finds its target. Clinical pharmacology becomes much easier when you master this basics!

question: Which of these is NOT a typical negative effect of widespread juvenile delinquency on society?

options.A: Destruction of public and private property
options.B: Surplus funding for educational infrastructure
options.C: Increased crime rates and community insecurity
options.D: Loss of productive human capital among youths

explanation: Well spotted! Delinquency drains money toward security and courts, so it definitely doesn't create extra funding for schools.

question: During which early stage of HIV do patients often experience flu-like symptoms and a high viral load?

options.A: AIDS stage
options.B: Acute HIV infection
options.C: Remission phase
options.D: Clinical latency

explanation: Right after exposure, the acute stage hits with lots of virus replication and mild flu-like signs. You're learning fast!

question: What is the main goal of Clinical Decision Support (CDS) alerts inside an EMR?

options.A: To schedule cleaning staff for patient rooms after discharge
options.B: To warn staff about drug allergies and dangerous interactions
options.C: To lock the computer screen if a nurse steps away too long
options.D: To calculate monthly hospital electricity and water bills

explanation: Think of CDS tools as a friendly safety net. They pop up to give you a heads-up if a prescribed drug clashes with a patient's known allergies.

question: Why is the active leadership of school management so important for a School Health Programme?

options.A: It allows administrators to practice medicine without a license
options.B: It eliminates the need for professional school nurses
options.C: It ensures that health policies remain strictly confidential
options.D: It provides the administrative backbone needed for proper coordination

explanation: You got it! School leaders have the official power and organization needed to guide and keep health activities running smoothly.

question: Which body landmark helps a clinician easily find the L4 spot for a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Center of the shoulder blades
options.B: Base of the neck vertebrae
options.C: Line connecting the iliac crests
options.D: Bottom edge of the ribcage

explanation: Correct! Drawing an imaginary line across the top of the hip bones (iliac crests) points right to the L4 space.

question: What does 'family food security' mean?

options.A: Having a locked storage room to protect food from insects
options.B: Having reliable access to enough safe, healthy food for everyone
options.C: Eating meals at the exact same time every single day
options.D: Growing all the family food on a private farm without buying anything

explanation: Food security simply means the household consistently has enough safe and nutritious food to live a healthy, active life.

question: What is the primary function of bile salts in digestion?

options.A: To digest complex proteins into amino acids
options.B: To neutralize the acidity of gastric chyme
options.C: To emulsify fats into smaller droplets
options.D: To stimulate the pancreas to release hormones

explanation: Bile salts break large fat globules down into tiny droplets, allowing lipase enzymes to work efficiently. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which of these is a common nursing diagnosis for a patient dealing with a reproductive disorder?

options.A: Ineffective tissue perfusion related to cardiac arrest
options.B: Excess fluid volume related to renal failure
options.C: Disturbed body image related to surgical alterations
options.D: Impaired gas exchange related to airway collapse

explanation: Spot on! Surgeries or issues involving reproductive organs can deeply affect how patients see themselves, making body image a key focus.

question: What is reported as the most common barrier to HIV disclosure?

options.A: Forgetting one's own diagnosis date
options.B: Lack of available transportation to the clinic
options.C: Excessive availability of antiretroviral drugs
options.D: Fear of stigma and discrimination

explanation: Societal prejudice and harsh judgment make people terrified of how others will treat them after learning their status. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h5)

question: Why should a patient with peripheral arterial disease be told not to put a hot water bottle directly on their feet?

options.A: External heat stops blood pressure medications from working
options.B: Poor feeling in the legs makes it easy to get bad burns without noticing
options.C: Heat can cause surface veins to collapse permanently
options.D: Warm temperatures make plaque grow faster

explanation: Because bad circulation can dull nerve feelings in the feet, patients might not realize the water is scalding hot until their skin is severely burned. Good clinical safety knowledge!

question: What is the best diagnostic test to confirm gout by spotting crystals directly?

options.A: Analysis of synovial fluid via arthrocentesis
options.B: Routine complete blood count with differential
options.C: Magnetic resonance imaging of the affected limb
options.D: Measurement of fasting serum glucose levels

explanation: Doctors confirm gout by drawing a small sample of fluid from the joint (arthrocentesis) and looking at it under a microscope to spot the crystals.

question: Which major body cavity contains both the heart and the lungs?

options.A: Thoracic cavity
options.B: Vertebral cavity
options.C: Abdominopelvic cavity
options.D: Cranial cavity

explanation: The thoracic cavity is located in the upper chest and houses the lungs, heart, and major blood vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h5)

question: What keeps the uterus bleeding heavily after an incomplete abortion?

options.A: The outer layer of the womb suddenly becomes very thick
options.B: The lower part of the womb closes up immediately
options.C: The uterine muscle fibers fail to contract tightly
options.D: The main blood vessels in the pelvis get blocked completely

explanation: When tissue stays trapped inside, the womb muscles can't squeeze down tightly to shut off the bleeding vessels. Makes total sense when you picture it!

question: What is a major benefit of connecting a visually impaired patient with a peer support group?

options.A: Diagnosing the underlying cause of their eye disease
options.B: Providing free medical treatments and prescription drugs
options.C: Sharing practical coping strategies and reducing isolation
options.D: Replacing the need for professional nursing home care

explanation: Spot on! Talking to others going through similar experiences helps patients feel less alone and gives them great everyday tips for living with low vision.

question: What is the main goal of planning a personal diet for a patient?

options.A: Reducing hospital food costs for the facility
options.B: Turning nutritional science into daily food choices
options.C: Eliminating all carbohydrates from the diet
options.D: Ensuring every patient eats the exact same calories

explanation: You're doing great! Diet planning simply takes nutrition rules from the textbook and translates them into the actual meals a person enjoys every day.

question: How long should children wash their hands with soap to properly get rid of germs?

options.A: Twenty seconds
options.B: Ten seconds
options.C: One hour
options.D: Two minutes

explanation: Twenty seconds is the magic number! Singing a short song helps kids scrub long enough to break down the germs on their skin.

question: When counseling pregnant women about traditional food habits, which approach is NOT helpful?

options.A: Listening carefully to the patient's family and cultural beliefs
options.B: Incorporating affordable local staples like beans and dark leafy greens
options.C: Identifying harmful taboos without disrespecting the community
options.D: Insisting that only imported foreign foods can provide proper prenatal nutrition

explanation: Spot on! Good nursing care relies on affordable, local foods that everyday families can actually get, not expensive foreign items.

question: Why are community health workers so helpful in managing family planning defaulters?

options.A: They manufacture all contraceptive drugs locally
options.B: They possess the legal power to arrest clients who miss appointments
options.C: They replace the need for physical clinics entirely
options.D: They can bridge the gap by reaching clients who cannot travel to the clinic

explanation: Community health workers extend our reach right into local neighborhoods, helping clients who find it hard to journey to the clinic.

question: What physical health issue is very common among child trafficking survivors?

options.A: Obesity and high blood pressure
options.B: Advanced neurological disorders
options.C: Congenital heart disease
options.D: Malnutrition and physical injuries

explanation: Victims are often denied proper food and face physical abuse, resulting in malnutrition and visible injuries.

question: Where would you expect to find an intramural fibroid?

options.A: On the outer surface of the uterus
options.B: Directly inside the uterine cavity lining
options.C: Inside the cervical canal
options.D: Within the muscular wall of the uterus

explanation: Think of 'intramural' as being right inside the walls—in this case, nestled comfortably within the muscular wall (myometrium) of the uterus.

question: What is the name of the painless sore that shows up during the first stage of syphilis?

options.A: Chancre
options.B: Pustule
options.C: Vesicle
options.D: Gumma

explanation: The classic early sign of syphilis is a firm, round, usually painless sore called a chancre right where the bacteria entered the skin.

question: What daily habit is most important for a patient with heart failure to spot early fluid buildup?

options.A: Testing their blood sugar levels
options.B: Checking their pulse every hour
options.C: Weighing themselves daily
options.D: Measuring their daily urine output

explanation: Spot on! A sudden jump on the scale is often the very first warning sign that the body is retaining fluid, so a daily weigh-in is a lifesaver.

question: Which nerve fibers send quick, sharp, 'ouch!' pain straight to your brain?

options.A: Autonomic fibers
options.B: C fibers
options.C: A-delta fibers
options.D: Motor neurons

explanation: Great job! A-delta fibers are wrapped in myelin (like an insulated wire), letting them zoom signals to your brain instantly when you get hurt.

question: Which of these is a major threat that can crash a Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: Issuing drugs on informal credit to friends and colleagues
options.B: Keeping the pharmacy windows open for ventilation
options.C: Writing clear dosage instructions on drug packs
options.D: Conducting weekly physical counts of medicine boxes

explanation: Giving drugs out on 'friendship credit' drains the cash drawer fast, making it impossible to restock. Business and friendly favors don't mix here!

question: Which chemical messenger is mainly responsible for the brain's reward system and feelings of pleasure during drug use?

options.A: Hemoglobin
options.B: Dopamine
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: Nailed it! Dopamine is our feel-good chemical. Drugs flood the brain with it, creating an intense artificial high that tricks the reward system.

question: A patient's blood pressure reads 142/92 mmHg in the clinic. Which category does this fall into?

options.A: Stage 1 Hypertension
options.B: Stage 2 Hypertension
options.C: Normal blood pressure
options.D: Elevated blood pressure

explanation: Since both the top number (142) is 140+ and the bottom number (92) is 90+, this climbs into Stage 2 hypertension.

question: What is the main purpose of a bag-valve-mask (BVM) resuscitator?

options.A: To measure blood oxygen saturation
options.B: To deliver positive pressure ventilation
options.C: To visualize the vocal cords clearly
options.D: To suction thick oral secretions

explanation: Great job! You squeeze the BVM manually to push air into the lungs of a patient who cannot breathe on their own. Simple and lifesaving! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h2)

question: Why might a patient with a badly damaged kidney have clear urine with no blood at all?

options.A: The blood supply or ureter to that kidney may be completely blocked or torn.
options.B: Blood from the injury goes directly into the stomach instead of the bladder.
options.C: The other healthy kidney absorbs all the blood before it reaches the urine.
options.D: The kidneys stop producing blood completely after a sudden physical impact.

explanation: If the tube carrying urine (the ureter) or the main blood vessel gets completely torn off, urine and blood from that injured kidney cannot flow down into the bladder. Makes sense, right?

question: What is a core duty of a nurse-midwife in promoting safe motherhood?

options.A: Avoiding community engagement activities
options.B: Focusing exclusively on administrative paperwork
options.C: Providing respectful maternity care and screening during antenatal visits
options.D: Discouraging women from visiting modern hospitals

explanation: As a nurse-midwife, you are a frontline hero! You screen mums, teach them what to expect, and always treat them with love and dignity.

question: If you eat more carbohydrates than your body needs right away, how is the extra sugar stored?

options.A: As free fatty acids floating in the spinal fluid
options.B: As liquid calcium deposits in the bone marrow
options.C: As glycogen in the liver and skeletal muscles
options.D: As raw amino acids inside the red blood cells

explanation: When there is extra sugar floating around, your liver and muscles quickly pack it together into a storage form called glycogen for later use.

question: What is the main goal of a fasting blood sugar test?

options.A: To find out the percentage of red blood cells carrying oxygen
options.B: To check how quickly the kidneys filter waste products
options.C: To measure blood sugar levels after a period without eating
options.D: To check the total amount of protein stored in the liver

explanation: You've got this! A fasting blood sugar test simply looks at your glucose levels after you haven't eaten for a while, usually overnight.

question: What is the proper technique for pulling a peripheral IV cannula out of a patient's skin?

options.A: Pull it out smoothly and parallel to the skin surface.
options.B: Twist the catheter in a full circle before lifting it out.
options.C: Tug it quickly and firmly to make the removal as fast as possible.
options.D: Pull it straight up toward the ceiling at a sharp 90-degree angle.

explanation: You've got it! Pulling it out smoothly and low to the skin prevents unnecessary scratching or trauma to the fragile vein wall.

question: How do nurses help fulfill a hospitalized patient's need for emotional safety?

options.A: By limiting visits from family members completely
options.B: By performing procedures quickly without warning
options.C: By keeping information about treatments a secret
options.D: By explaining procedures clearly and answering questions honestly

explanation: Clear communication reduces anxiety and helps patients feel secure and in control of their situation. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h4)

question: A weightlifter performing heavy one-rep maximum lifts relies primarily on which muscle fiber type?

options.A: Cardiac muscle fibers
options.B: Fast glycolytic fibers
options.C: Smooth muscle fibers
options.D: Slow oxidative fibers

explanation: Fast glycolytic fibers generate quick, powerful contractions using anaerobic pathways, perfect for heavy lifting and short sprints. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h7)

question: Which of these conditions is most likely to need a surgical valve repair or replacement?

options.A: Simple ventricular ectopic beats
options.B: Severe aortic stenosis
options.C: Controlled essential hypertension
options.D: Mild sinus tachycardia

explanation: When a valve is severely narrowed (stenosis), blood can't get through properly. Surgery is often needed to fix or replace that physical blockage.

question: Which sign tells you there might be nerve compression in a limb with skin traction?

options.A: Rapid healing of the skin surface
options.B: Dark brown discoloration of the nails
options.C: Increased warmth and heavy sweating
options.D: Numbness and tingling in the toes

explanation: Numbness and tingling (paresthesia) are classic warning signs that pressure is building up on the nerves. Always listen when patients report these feelings!

question: A nurse wants to study the shared daily habits and culture of nurses in a busy emergency room. Which research approach fits best?

options.A: Phenomenology
options.B: Grounded theory
options.C: Ethnography
options.D: Randomized controlled trial

explanation: Brilliant! Ethnography is like diving into a specific cultural or social group to understand their shared workplace habits and lifestyle.

question: In the SBAR communication tool, what does the letter 'B' stand for?

options.A: Bedside
options.B: Background
options.C: Behavior
options.D: Balance

explanation: Awesome! 'B' is for Background, which gives the history and context leading up to the current situation.

question: How do Integrase Strand Transfer Inhibitors (INSTIs) stop HIV from multiplying?

options.A: By destroying red blood cells in the bloodstream
options.B: By preventing viral DNA from inserting into the host cell's DNA
options.C: By changing the patient's blood type permanently
options.D: By blocking the patient from feeling hungry

explanation: You got it! INSTIs block the 'integrase' enzyme, which the virus uses like glue to paste its own genetic code into our human cells.

question: What is the main goal of pressure redistribution for patients who spend all day in bed?

options.A: Accelerating the breakdown of red blood cells
options.B: Increasing the overall room temperature
options.C: Spreading body weight to protect delicate skin
options.D: Making it easier to change hospital pajamas

explanation: That's correct! Spreading weight across a larger surface area takes the harsh, concentrated pressure off bony areas, helping to keep the skin safe and healthy.

question: What happens to the amount of virus (viral load) during the long, quiet chronic latency stage of HIV?

options.A: It drops to lower levels compared to the acute stage
options.B: It increases rapidly every single day
options.C: It remains exactly identical to the acute stage peak
options.D: It disappears completely from the bloodstream

explanation: Great job! During latency, the viral load settles down compared to the massive spike during early infection, though the virus is still quietly active.

question: How often should you check a mother's vital signs while she is stabilizing after a postpartum hemorrhage?

options.A: Every 30 seconds
options.B: Every 2 hours
options.C: Only once before leaving
options.D: Every 15 minutes

explanation: Checking every 15 minutes lets you catch early signs of shock or ongoing bleeding before they become life-threatening.

question: An older male patient with an enlarged prostate experiences constant urinary dribbling because his bladder is completely full. What is this called?

options.A: Overflow incontinence
options.B: Urge urinary incontinence
options.C: Stress urinary incontinence
options.D: Functional incontinence

explanation: When a blockage stops the bladder from emptying properly, it overfills and leaks small amounts. We call this overflow incontinence. Excellent nursing insight!

question: Why are fallopian tubes easily reached by infections starting in the lower vagina or cervix?

options.A: They lack any blood supply to fight off invading microorganisms
options.B: They produce constant secretions that feed bacterial pathogens
options.C: They share a continuous open mucosal pathway with the uterus and cervix
options.D: They are located outside the main pelvic cavity entirely

explanation: Because the female reproductive tract is an open road from the vagina up through the uterus and tubes, bacteria can easily travel upward.

question: Which leadership style uses a system of rewards and punishments to manage staff?

options.A: Authentic leadership
options.B: Situational leadership
options.C: Transformational leadership
options.D: Transactional leadership

explanation: Think 'transaction'—you do this task well, you get rewarded; you make a mistake, you face correction. That's transactional leadership!

question: Why should nurses avoid applying urban health assumptions directly to rural farming communities in Nigeria?

options.A: Rural and urban populations often have very different physical activity levels and dietary realities
options.B: Medical diagnostic equipment is completely unavailable outside major state capitals
options.C: Rural communities are completely immune to lifestyle-related chronic health conditions
options.D: Urban residents never participate in focus group discussions or health interviews

explanation: You nailed it! City life and village life are completely different. What works for an office worker in Lagos might make zero sense for a farmer in a rural community.

question: Why is it so important to give Parkinson's medications right on time?

options.A: To build up a lifelong immunity against tremors
options.B: To ensure the medication permanently cures the brain disease
options.C: To prevent sudden 'wearing-off' periods where motor symptoms return
options.D: To stop the patient from ever feeling sleepy during the day

explanation: Parkinson's meds have a very specific window of action. If a dose is delayed, the protective levels drop quickly, and stiffness or tremors can rapidly return.

question: What is widely considered the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in a hospital?

options.A: Wearing heavy utility gloves all day
options.B: Spraying chemical disinfectants on walls
options.C: Keeping all windows wide open
options.D: Consistent and proper hand hygiene

explanation: Good old handwashing (or using an alcohol rub) is your superpower. It stops germs dead in their tracks before they reach you or your next patient.

question: What is the main difference between good (appropriate) polypharmacy and bad (problematic) polypharmacy?

options.A: Problematic polypharmacy only occurs in hospital intensive care units.
options.B: Problematic polypharmacy means the patient refuses to swallow pills.
options.C: Appropriate polypharmacy has clear clinical benefits that outweigh risks.
options.D: Appropriate polypharmacy involves only traditional herbal mixtures.

explanation: Taking many drugs isn't always bad if every single pill has a clear job that helps the patient more than it harms them. That's appropriate polypharmacy!

question: What is the primary purpose of a Glucose Tolerance Test?

options.A: To measure how the body clears a glucose load over time
options.B: To evaluate how quickly the kidneys filter sugar from the blood
options.C: To measure the exact amount of insulin stored in the pancreas
options.D: To determine the average blood sugar level over the past three months

explanation: The GTT tracks how effectively the body processes and clears a specific amount of glucose over several hours. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h1)

question: Why is mental health and psychological support so important for patients with long-term autoimmune conditions?

options.A: Patients with autoimmune diseases lose their memory over time
options.B: Mental stress is proven to be the sole biological cause of all autoimmune flares
options.C: Psychological counseling replaces the need for anti-inflammatory medications
options.D: Coping with chronic, unpredictable physical illness often leads to anxiety and depression

explanation: Living with unpredictable pain and tiredness is mentally exhausting. Caring for the whole patient means supporting their mind as well as their body!

question: When is the best time to check the psychosocial needs of a patient with a chronic blood disorder?

options.A: Exclusively on the first day of the initial hospital visit
options.B: Whenever the patient requests a change in their medication
options.C: As an ongoing process throughout the course of the illness
options.D: Only during the final stage of palliative care admission

explanation: A patient's worries change as their illness progresses. Checking in regularly lets you catch new stress early!

question: In many rural Nigerian communities, who is usually the very first person consulted when someone falls ill?

options.A: Hospital laboratory scientists
options.B: Consultant surgeons
options.C: University pharmacists
options.D: Traditional practitioners

explanation: Because traditional healers and birth attendants are trusted and easy to reach in rural areas, people often visit them first before coming to a modern clinic.

question: Which cranial nerve brings most of the sensory messages from our entire face?

options.A: Facial nerve
options.B: Vagus nerve
options.C: Trigeminal nerve
options.D: Glossopharyngeal nerve

explanation: You got it! The trigeminal nerve (CN V) is the big sensory highway for our face, divided into three helpful branches.

question: What is usually the very first step public health teams take when investigating a suspected disease outbreak?

options.A: Hold a press conference on national television
options.B: Close down all schools and markets in the entire country
options.C: Burn medical waste to destroy any remaining bacteria
options.D: Verify the diagnosis and confirm that an outbreak actually exists

explanation: Correct! Before launching a full investigation, health workers must make sure laboratory results and case numbers truly point to an outbreak.

question: Which past medical history is most important when assessing a male patient's fertility risks?

options.A: A normal resting heart rate and blood pressure reading
options.B: A history of undescended testicles in childhood
options.C: A personal preference for wearing loose cotton clothing
options.D: Occasional mild muscle soreness after heavy exercise

explanation: Undescended testicles mean the tissue spent time exposed to higher core body heat, which can impact future fertility. Great clinical insight to keep in mind!

question: A confused patient arrives at the emergency ward. What is one of the quickest bedside checks you should do?

options.A: A random blood glucose check
options.B: A twenty-four-hour urine collection
options.C: A complete neurological reflex test
options.D: A fasting lipid profile test

explanation: Always check blood sugar when a patient's mental status changes. It takes seconds to rule out severe hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, which can look just like confusion!

question: What is the main goal of evaluating an IEC campaign after it has ended?

options.A: The speed at which the community health extension workers walk
options.B: Whether community knowledge increased and health practices actually changed
options.C: The exact cost of ink used to print the educational leaflets
options.D: How many posters were torn down by heavy rainfall and wind

explanation: Evaluation lets you know if your hard work paid off by checking if people actually learned something new and changed their health habits for the better.

question: When is the best time to give antiemetic (anti-nausea) medication to a palliative patient who struggles with nausea at meal times?

options.A: Right before bedtime
options.B: Only when the patient falls asleep
options.C: Right after finishing a large plate
options.D: Before meals

explanation: Well reasoned! Giving the anti-nausea medicine ahead of time stops nausea before it starts, helping the patient actually enjoy a few bites of food.

question: What is a main goal of couples counseling when treating female sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Legally binding the couple to a specific treatment plan
options.B: Improving communication and reducing performance anxiety
options.C: Performing physical examinations on both partners together
options.D: Prescribing precise hormonal dosages for the female partner

explanation: You're doing great! Counseling helps partners talk openly, take off the pressure of strict expectations, and grow closer together.

question: Which medical term is used for a freely movable joint?

options.A: Synarthrosis
options.B: Syndesmosis
options.C: Amphiarthrosis
options.D: Diarthrosis

explanation: Well done! A 'diarthrosis' is a freely movable joint (think of your dancing hips or swinging arms). It matches up with our synovial joints.

question: Why are progestin-only implants safer for women with a history of blood clots compared to combined oral pills?

options.A: They actively dissolve existing blood clots within the deep veins
options.B: They completely destroy all circulating red blood cells in the body
options.C: They bypass the liver entirely and go straight into the heart muscle
options.D: They do not contain estrogen, which is the main hormone linked to clotting risks

explanation: Estrogen is usually the troublemaker when it comes to blood clots in contraceptives. Since implants are progestin-only, they leave estrogen out of the picture!

question: Why must an antiseptic skin prep air-dry completely before inserting an IV catheter?

options.A: To allow the chemical time to kill microorganisms effectively
options.B: To ensure the vein stays dilated and easy to see
options.C: To prevent the sticky dressing from sliding off wet skin
options.D: To keep the patient from feeling a burning sensation

explanation: Antiseptics like chlorhexidine require contact time and drying to achieve their full germ-killing effect. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the most effective way for nurses to help prevent unsafe abortions in the community?

options.A: Providing accessible family planning education and modern contraception
options.B: Reporting all suspected cases of premarital sex to local community elders
options.C: Enforcing strict hospital visitation limits for young unmarried females
options.D: Promoting traditional herbal remedies as safe alternatives for fertility control

explanation: The best cure is prevention! When young people have easy access to modern family planning and accurate education, the rate of unintended pregnancies—and unsafe abortions—drops dramatically.

question: What is a notable disadvantage of topical drug administration?

options.A: It is impossible to use if the patient has a functioning gastrointestinal tract
options.B: Absorption can be unpredictable due to skin thickness and condition
options.C: It causes immediate and severe first-pass liver failure every time
options.D: It always requires sterile operating room conditions to apply

explanation: Because skin condition, hydration, and thickness vary across the body and between patients, absorption rates can be inconsistent. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h5)

question: Where do water-soluble hormones usually find their receptors?

options.A: On the outer cell surface
options.B: Inside the cell nucleus
options.C: Inside the mitochondrial matrix
options.D: Floating freely in the blood

explanation: Because water-soluble hormones can't slip right through the oily cell membrane, they latch onto receptors sitting on the outside of the cell to pass their message along! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h1)

question: Which specific pelvic joint is most directly affected by symphysis pubis dysfunction?

options.A: The knee hinge joint
options.B: The hip socket joint
options.C: The ankle mortise joint
options.D: The pubic symphysis joint

explanation: Symphysis pubis dysfunction causes pain right at the front pubic joint where the two pelvic bones meet. It's a common area of discomfort!

question: In the HEADSS adolescent screening tool, what does the letter 'S' stand for?

options.A: Suicide and Safety
options.B: Social status
options.C: Sleeping habits
options.D: Skeletal strength

explanation: Spot on! The last section of the HEADSS framework focuses on Suicide risks, depression, and overall Safety behaviors.

question: What is the main goal of having a multi-sectoral referral network for GBV survivors?

options.A: To provide comprehensive medical, legal, and social support through coordinated agencies
options.B: To reduce the total number of follow-up medical visits required
options.C: To transfer all administrative responsibilities away from the hospital
options.D: To ensure the police handle every aspect of the patient's recovery

explanation: Healing takes a village! Teamwork between health workers, legal aid, and social services gives survivors the best all-round support.

question: What are the three main parts of the brain stem, arranged from top to bottom?

options.A: Pons, medulla oblongata, and spinal cord
options.B: Cerebrum, cerebellum, and spinal cord
options.C: Midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata
options.D: Thalamus, hypothalamus, and midbrain

explanation: Think of the brain stem in three neat sections: the midbrain sits up top, the pons is right in the middle, and the medulla oblongata is at the bottom leading right into the spinal cord. You've got this!

question: Which protein in the blood is the main carrier for drugs?

options.A: Albumin
options.B: Globulin
options.C: Fibrinogen
options.D: Hemoglobin

explanation: Albumin is the most common protein in our blood plasma. It acts like a taxi service, carrying many different drugs around the body.

question: Why should a nurse apply pressure to an IV site immediately after withdrawing the catheter?

options.A: To ensure the plastic catheter tip remains intact inside the arm.
options.B: To push any remaining trapped air bubbles back up into the vein.
options.C: To stimulate rapid skin healing and eliminate scarring completely.
options.D: To stop bleeding and prevent hematoma formation at the site.

explanation: Applying direct pressure helps seal the puncture wound in the blood vessel wall, stopping external bleeding and preventing internal bruising. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h8)

question: Why do doctors prescribe antidiabetic medications for patients with diabetes mellitus?

options.A: To restore normal metabolic balance and lower blood sugar
options.B: To permanently replace the need for dietary modifications
options.C: To stimulate the continuous release of stored glucagon
options.D: To completely cure the underlying pancreatic disease

explanation: You got it! These drugs help keep blood glucose in check to prevent long-term complications, even though they aren't a permanent cure on their own.

question: What goes wrong if you crush an extended-release capsule before giving it to a patient?

options.A: The medication will take twice as long to work
options.B: The entire dose is released at once, risking toxicity
options.C: The patient will experience no therapeutic effect
options.D: The active ingredients are completely destroyed

explanation: Crushing destroys the special timed-release design. Instead of a steady, safe trickle of medicine over hours, the patient gets a dangerous flood all at once!

question: Why should we worry when livestock farmers use antibiotics too frequently?

options.A: It causes animals to stop producing milk entirely
options.B: It can contribute to antimicrobial resistance
options.C: It turns the meat a bright green color
options.D: It makes the meat taste bitter to consumers

explanation: Overusing antibiotics on animals creates tougher, resistant germs that can eventually spread to humans and shrug off our best medications.

question: What kind of tumor grows into nearby tissues and travels to other parts of the body?

options.A: Benign tumor
options.B: Metaplastic lesion
options.C: Malignant tumor
options.D: Hyperplastic growth

explanation: Spot on! Malignant tumors are cancerous because they don't stay in one place—they can invade local tissues and travel through the blood or lymph to other parts of the body.

question: What happens to a diagnostic skin test if the nurse accidentally injects the medication into the subcutaneous layer?

options.A: The medication crystallizes under the skin and causes infection.
options.B: The patient develops immediate anaphylactic shock.
options.C: The reaction becomes much larger and easier to read.
options.D: The test becomes invalid because the drug absorbs too quickly.

explanation: Subcutaneous tissue has more blood supply, causing rapid absorption that ruins the localized delayed immune reaction needed for a valid test. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h6)

question: What type of care approach is most effective when treating survivors of forced marriage?

options.A: Experimental surgical care
options.B: Strictly punitive care
options.C: Cosmetic dermatological care
options.D: Trauma-informed care

explanation: Trauma-informed care acknowledges the profound psychological impact of abuse and focuses on safety, trust, and empowerment for the survivor. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h7)

question: A patient with a degenerative condition frequently becomes exhausted halfway through a morning walk. What physical therapy strategy should be introduced?

options.A: Energy conservation and activity pacing
options.B: Complete bed rest to eliminate all physical exertion
options.C: Immediate removal of all walking aids
options.D: High-intensity weight lifting to build sudden bulk

explanation: Teaching the patient to pace themselves and conserve energy helps them stay active without burning out all their strength at once. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h4)

question: What does the clinical term 'polypharmacy' mean?

options.A: The delivery of drugs through an intravenous line
options.B: The concurrent use of multiple medications by a patient
options.C: The process of mixing liquid medicines with food
options.D: The manufacturing of generic drugs by large pharmacies

explanation: Polypharmacy simply means taking several medications at once. It's very common in older adults and increases the risk of side effects and dangerous drug interactions.

question: How can a father directly support good child nutrition at home?

options.A: By mixing infant formula with fresh cow milk
options.B: By providing funds for diverse and nutritious food items
options.C: By growing all the household crops by himself
options.D: By deciding the exact feeding times for the mother

explanation: Providing money to buy quality, healthy food is one of the best ways fathers contribute to child nutrition.

question: What is the main focus of a physical therapist visiting a patient at home?

options.A: Providing emotional counseling for grief
options.B: Assisting with daily grocery shopping
options.C: Restoring physical mobility and strength
options.D: Managing complex intravenous drug dosages

explanation: Correct! Physiotherapists help patients get moving again so they can regain their balance and daily strength.

question: What is an effective way to help a hypertensive patient reduce their sodium intake?

options.A: Telling them to completely stop eating all forms of food
options.B: Advise them to rely entirely on restaurant meals
options.C: Suggesting they double their daily intake of canned foods
options.D: Teaching them how to read food labels and use herbs instead of salt

explanation: Practical education gives patients actionable tools like label reading and alternative flavorings to manage their health successfully. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h7)

question: How do common antipyretic drugs like paracetamol primarily lower a fever?

options.A: By blocking prostaglandin synthesis in the brain
options.B: By destroying bacteria in the bloodstream
options.C: By forcing the blood vessels in the skin to constrict
options.D: By directly cooling the skin through evaporation

explanation: Antipyretics stop the production of prostaglandins in the hypothalamus, which allows the body's internal thermostat to drop back down. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T3#GNS221_U3_T3_h4)

question: If you are working right next to active X-ray or C-arm machines in the theatre, what protective wear must you wear?

options.A: Sterile waterproof surgical gowns
options.B: Thick rubber washing gloves
options.C: N95 nose masks
options.D: Lead aprons and thyroid shields

explanation: Radiation from imaging machines is powerful stuff! We use dense barriers like lead aprons and shields to keep our tissues safe from harm.

question: What long-term heart problem often develops from chronic, untreated severe anemia?

options.A: Primary pulmonary hypertension
options.B: High-output heart failure
options.C: Chronic deep vein thrombosis
options.D: Peripheral artery disease

explanation: Imagine running a car engine at top speed every single day—eventually, it wears out. The heart muscle gets exhausted from constantly overworking to pump oxygen-poor blood, leading to heart failure.

question: What is the main job of checkpoints in the normal cell cycle?

options.A: To stop division if DNA damage is found
options.B: To speed up tissue growth
options.C: To provide energy for the cell to split
options.D: To turn active cells into resting cells

explanation: Great try! Cell checkpoints act like security guards—they inspect the cell and halt the cycle if anything looks damaged, keeping the body safe.

question: What should happen to a palliative care plan as the patient's disease progresses?

options.A: It should be updated dynamically to reflect changing needs and wishes
options.B: It is handed over entirely to family members to manage at home
options.C: It must remain exactly as written on admission day to avoid confusion
options.D: It should be closed and archived once the patient becomes too weak to talk

explanation: Since palliative needs change constantly, our care plans must be flexible and updated regularly by the healthcare team.

question: What does 'clinical significance' mean in simple terms when looking at drug research?

options.A: Whether the research paper was published in an international journal
options.B: Whether the study results make a meaningful, noticeable difference to the patient's health
options.C: Whether the pharmaceutical company made a profit from the drug trial
options.D: Whether the mathematical formula used in the data analysis was complex enough

explanation: Well done! Numbers might show a tiny statistical change, but clinical significance means the patient actually feels or gets better in real life.

question: Why do hospital policies play a big role in what you are allowed to do during clinicals?

options.A: They dictate what nursing students are legally permitted to perform on patients
options.B: They set the tuition fees for the university nursing department
options.C: They determine the exact colors of the school uniforms
options.D: They write all the final examinations for the nursing council

explanation: Hospitals have strict rules to protect patients and keep student practice within safe, legal boundaries.

question: When must the very first baseline swab count be done?

options.A: When the patient enters the recovery ward
options.B: After the surgical wound is closed
options.C: Only if an extra pack is requested
options.D: Before the surgery begins

explanation: You have to know your starting point! The baseline count happens before any incision is made.

question: What is the main difference between simple diffusion and facilitated diffusion?

options.A: Simple diffusion moves nutrients against a gradient, while facilitated moves with it
options.B: Simple diffusion only moves water, while facilitated diffusion moves solids
options.C: Simple diffusion requires ATP, while facilitated diffusion does not
options.D: Simple diffusion does not use carrier proteins, while facilitated diffusion does

explanation: Think of simple diffusion as slipping easily through a gap, while facilitated diffusion needs special protein 'doorkeepers' to help molecules across the membrane.

question: In nursing, what does the common acronym ADL stand for?

options.A: Advanced Dietary List
options.B: Alternate Drug Logistics
options.C: Activities of Daily Living
options.D: Acute Disease Level

explanation: You nailed it! ADLs are the everyday things we do to care for ourselves, like bathing, dressing, and eating.

question: Which of the following is a direct obstetric complication linked to female genital mutilation?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Obstructed labor and tearing
options.C: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.D: Hyperemesis gravidarum severity

explanation: Scar tissue from these practices restricts the birth canal, leading to difficult deliveries and severe tearing. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h2)

question: Why are patients told to avoid signing important legal documents for 24 hours after a sedated endoscopy?

options.A: Hospitals are legally liable for outside contracts signed.
options.B: Sedative drugs can temporarily impair judgment and memory.
options.C: The bright lights in the procedure room damage eye muscles.
options.D: Anesthesia causes permanent changes in logical thinking.

explanation: Even if they feel completely awake, leftover sedation affects clear thinking and memory, so making major choices can wait until the next day.

question: A young girl is brought to the emergency department hours after undergoing FGM, presenting with an inability to pass urine and extreme lower abdominal swelling. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Urethral obstruction from local tissue swelling and pain spasm
options.B: Diabetic ketoacidosis affecting renal function
options.C: Primary kidney failure due to congenital anomalies
options.D: Severe dehydration from lack of drinking water

explanation: Acute trauma and inflammation around the vulva commonly cause urinary retention due to mechanical blockage and fear of pain during micturition. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the term for long-term liver damage caused by repeated inflammation and severe scarring?

options.A: Cholelithiasis
options.B: Steatosis
options.C: Cirrhosis
options.D: Necrosis

explanation: You're doing great! Over time, constant scarring replaces healthy liver tissue with tough fibrous tissue. We call this condition cirrhosis.

question: What is the primary purpose of bereavement support after a patient passes away?

options.A: To disinfect the hospital room according to policy
options.B: To complete hospital discharge billing procedures quickly
options.C: To help surviving family members process their grief and cope with loss
options.D: To determine the exact legal cause of death for insurance

explanation: Bereavement support extends palliative care principles to the family after death, assisting them through the normal grieving process. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h7)

question: Which type of distributive shock is typically associated with a slow heart rate (bradycardia)?

options.A: Hypovolemic shock
options.B: Neurogenic shock
options.C: Anaphylactic shock
options.D: Septic shock

explanation: Spinal cord injuries disrupt sympathetic nervous pathways, leaving vagal tone unopposed and causing a surprisingly slow pulse. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h5)

question: Why would a doctor order a tympanometry test?

options.A: To test the patient's balance and coordination
options.B: To check middle ear function and detect fluid
options.C: To measure the electrical activity of the brain
options.D: To visualize the tiny bones of the inner ear directly

explanation: Tympanometry tests how well your eardrum moves when air pressure changes. It's great for spotting fluid or pressure issues behind the eardrum.

question: What sensation should you warn a patient to expect when the barium liquid goes in?

options.A: Total numbness from the waist down to the toes
options.B: Heavy sleepiness and deep drowsiness
options.C: A sharp burning feeling across the skin of the belly
options.D: A strong urge to use the toilet and mild belly cramps

explanation: Filling the large intestine with fluid naturally creates pressure and triggers bowel contractions. Giving patients a heads-up helps ease their anxiety.

question: Which problem-solving model focuses on looking backward after an error to find underlying system failures?

options.A: Random brainstorming
options.B: Trial and error
options.C: Immediate punishment
options.D: Root cause analysis

explanation: Root cause analysis investigates why an incident happened by looking at underlying workplace or system processes. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h4)

question: A high level of uric acid in the blood is a major clue for doctors diagnosing which condition?

options.A: Bone fracture
options.B: Osteoporosis
options.C: Muscle atrophy
options.D: Gout

explanation: Gout happens when uric acid crystals build up in the joints. Checking blood uric acid is a fast way to spot it!

question: Which of these is a great example of secondary data in a community assessment?

options.A: Focus group discussions with local market women
options.B: Direct visual observations of village water sources
options.C: Interviews conducted by nurses during home visits
options.D: Clinic registers and existing census reports

explanation: Spot on! Secondary data is information that was already collected by someone else and is sitting in existing records and reports.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical safety hazard inside an operating room?

options.A: Sharps injuries from needles and scalpel blades
options.B: Electrical risks from high-powered surgical equipment
options.C: Chemical exposure from waste anesthetic gases
options.D: High-speed public traffic noise from outside the hospital

explanation: You got it! Operating rooms are quiet and sound-proofed. The real worries inside are things like sharps, chemicals, and electrical hazards.

question: Which of these is NOT a rule for the lactational amenorrhea method (LAM) to work as birth control?

options.A: The infant must be over one year old
options.B: The baby must be under six months of age
options.C: The mother's menses must not have returned
options.D: The mother must exclusively breastfeed

explanation: LAM only works for babies under six months old who are exclusively breastfed and whose monthly periods have not returned yet.

question: Why do calming or sedating medications increase the risk of choking in older adults?

options.A: They can dull the natural swallowing reflex and cause drowsiness.
options.B: They weaken the muscles of the arms, preventing self-feeding.
options.C: They completely dry out the lining of the esophagus permanently.
options.D: They cause the stomach to expand and push food back upward.

explanation: Spot on! When someone is very drowsy, their body's reflexes slow down, making it hard to coordinate chewing and swallowing safely.

question: Why should you always talk to an unconscious patient before doing a procedure?

options.A: To wake the patient up immediately from a coma
options.B: To prove to the family that the nurse is working
options.C: Because hearing is the last sense to disappear
options.D: To maintain dignity and acknowledge their presence

explanation: Never lose sight of the person! Even if they can't answer, talking to them shows respect and preserves their human dignity.

question: Why do dying patients often get cool, pale, and mottled hands and feet?

options.A: Lack of oxygen forces the lungs to shut down blood flow to the limbs
options.B: Kidney failure causes excess fluid to accumulate under the skin layers
options.C: The patient is experiencing a sudden and severe drop in environmental temperature
options.D: The heart loses the ability to pump blood effectively to peripheral tissues

explanation: As the body slows down, it naturally prioritizes sending blood to vital organs like the brain and heart, leaving the hands and feet cool to the touch.

question: Which government bodies usually set the rules for healthcare waste management?

options.A: Ministries of health and environmental agencies
options.B: Patient advocacy groups and volunteer clubs
options.C: Local taxi drivers unions and market associations
options.D: Private pharmaceutical manufacturing companies

explanation: Well done! Government health and environmental sectors hold the legal duty to set safety standards for everyone.

question: What is one effective strategy to ensure two-way communication in a referral system?

options.A: Banning clients from ever returning to their original health post
options.B: Using standardized feedback forms sent back by the receiving facility
options.C: Destroying all medical records once a client leaves the primary clinic
options.D: Stopping all phone calls between hospitals and primary centers

explanation: Two-way feedback forms allow receiving hospitals to report back to the referring nurse on the client's outcome. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of building 'herd immunity' through mass vaccination campaigns?

options.A: Ensuring that pharmaceutical companies sell out their entire drug supply
options.B: Removing the need for clean drinking water and proper waste disposal
options.C: Completely eliminating all microorganisms from the natural environment
options.D: Protecting vulnerable community members by making transmission difficult

explanation: Spot on! When most of the community is vaccinated, the germ struggles to find new hosts, which keeps the few unvaccinated or vulnerable people safe too.

question: What is the primary role of a critical care nurse during patient assessment?

options.A: Prescribing emergency medications independently
options.B: Performing surgical interventions at the bedside
options.C: Replacing laboratory diagnostic equipment
options.D: Detecting subtle physiological changes early

explanation: The critical care nurse serves as a continuous observer to catch small warning signs before a patient deteriorates fully. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T2#GNS321_U2_T2_h1)

question: What is a major disadvantage of bilateral tubal ligation compared to barrier methods like condoms?

options.A: It requires daily motivation and adherence from the client.
options.B: It immediately causes early menopause and hot flashes.
options.C: It has a very high failure rate within the first year.
options.D: It offers no protection against sexually transmitted infections.

explanation: While highly effective at preventing pregnancy, tubal ligation does not shield against sexually transmitted infections, unlike barrier methods. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h7)

question: In some traditional settings, why are eggs and chicken meat sometimes withheld from young children?

options.A: Lack of available cooking oil in rural markets
options.B: Strict government laws against eating farm birds
options.C: Fear of causing speech delays, greed, or stubbornness
options.D: Belief that poultry meat causes high blood pressure

explanation: It's a common local myth! Elders sometimes worry that letting kids eat chicken or eggs will make them greedy or delay their talking. As nurses, we gently educate against this.

question: What information does the vestibular cortex primarily process?

options.A: High-pitched sounds and spoken speech
options.B: Balance, motion, and spatial orientation
options.C: Written words and visual colors
options.D: Chemical flavors and food textures

explanation: The vestibular system and its cortical region handle equilibrium, head position, and movement through space. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T11#GNS211_U3_T11_h6)

question: What is the very first priority when managing a patient who presents with acute shock?

options.A: Restoring adequate airway, breathing, and circulation
options.B: Preparing the patient for major exploratory surgery
options.C: Lowering the body temperature with cooling blankets
options.D: Administering broad-spectrum oral antibiotics immediately

explanation: Always remember your ABCs! No matter what kind of shock it is, emergency care always starts with securing the airway, breathing, and circulation before digging into secondary causes.

question: How does pulmonary tuberculosis usually spread from one person to another?

options.A: By sharing eating utensils
options.B: Through direct skin-to-skin contact
options.C: Through contaminated drinking water
options.D: By airborne droplet nuclei

explanation: TB travels through tiny droplets in the air when someone with active TB coughs or sneezes. That's why breathing the same enclosed air can lead to infection.

question: What are some common emotional reactions a client might experience after an abortion?

options.A: Uncontrollable happiness and laughter
options.B: Complete physical paralysis
options.C: Relief, sadness, or guilt
options.D: Total loss of memory

explanation: Emotions are complex and vary widely. A client might feel relief, sorrow, or a mixture of many things—and all of these responses can be completely normal. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h6)

question: Why are greenstick fractures much more common in young children than in adults?

options.A: Children have softer and more flexible bones
options.B: Children lack calcium in their diet entirely
options.C: Children have thicker skin protecting their limbs
options.D: Children fall with much greater velocity

explanation: Immature pediatric bones tend to bend and splinter on one side rather than snapping completely in two, much like a fresh green tree branch. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h2)

question: What is the job of the thermopile inside an infrared thermometer?

options.A: It blocks bright room light from entering
options.B: It warms up the lens to match body heat
options.C: It pumps cool air over the computer chips
options.D: It converts absorbed heat into an electrical signal

explanation: Think of the thermopile as a translator: it takes the focused heat energy and turns it into an electrical voltage that the thermometer's screen can read.

question: What is the term for a resting heart rate that drops below 60 beats per minute?

options.A: Tachypnea
options.B: Bradycardia
options.C: Hypotension
options.D: Tachycardia

explanation: Bradycardia simply means a slow heart rate (under 60 bpm in adults). You are building a strong clinical vocabulary! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h8)

question: Why is communication different in a community setting compared to a busy hospital ward?

options.A: Community nurses only use written notes instead of talking
options.B: Hospital patients never need verbal health instructions
options.C: Hospital care relies entirely on non-verbal body signs
options.D: Community nurses build long-term relationships with families

explanation: Because community nurses work closely with the same neighborhoods and families over time, their communication focuses heavily on long-term relationships and prevention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h1)

question: A client vomits twenty minutes after drinking the glucose beverage. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Proceed with the remaining blood draws because enough sugar was absorbed
options.B: Notify the laboratory and physician that the test must be rescheduled
options.C: Collect blood samples on an accelerated schedule to make up for lost time
options.D: Have the client drink a second dose of glucose immediately and continue

explanation: Vomiting means an unknown amount of glucose was absorbed, making the test results invalid; it must be rescheduled for another day. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h4)

question: Why do many traditional taboos give the best pieces of meat to adult males instead of children?

options.A: Cultural hierarchy assigns priority foods to providers and leaders
options.B: Adult males require more physical energy to farm and hunt
options.C: Children's digestive systems cannot process animal protein
options.D: Meat spoils faster when eaten by younger family members

explanation: Traditional power structures often dictate that heads of households and male breadwinners receive the most prized food items first.

question: What is the primary focus of social services in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Performing major orthopedic surgeries in the operating theatre
options.B: Addressing non-medical social and economic challenges affecting health
options.C: Conducting laboratory blood tests and urinalysis
options.D: Prescribing strong antibiotics for bacterial infections

explanation: Good health isn't just about medicine! Social services look at things like poverty, living conditions, and family support that affect how well a patient recovers.

question: What term is used to measure the amount of tracer absorbed in a specific spot on a PET scan?

options.A: Systemic Urine Volume
options.B: Standardized Uptake Value
options.C: Specific Ultrasound Velocity
options.D: Serum Utilization Variable

explanation: You got it! Radiologists use the Standardized Uptake Value (SUV) as a handy number to measure just how much tracer activity is happening in a specific tissue.

question: What is the primary danger of delaying or ignoring routine infrastructure maintenance in a hospital?

options.A: It always results in immediate promotion for the maintenance director
options.B: It forces the hospital to switch entirely to paperless documentation
options.C: It automatically increases the total number of available hospital beds
options.D: It can lead to equipment failure, safety hazards, and regulatory penalties

explanation: Putting off repairs creates hidden dangers that can harm patients or staff, and it leads to failing official health inspections. Keeping things fixed keeps everyone safe!

question: What is the main goal of infection control when caring for patients right inside their own homes?

options.A: Eliminating all microorganisms from the domestic environment
options.B: Transforming the private home into a sterile hospital room
options.C: Reducing the cost of medical equipment maintenance
options.D: Breaking the chain of infection to protect clients and workers

explanation: Spot on! The big picture in home care is always stopping germs from spreading between you and your patient. You've got this!

question: Why do the very first cell divisions (cleavage) happen without the embryo getting physically larger?

options.A: The mother's bloodstream actively starves the embryo of extra water
options.B: The embryo remains constrained inside the protective zona pellucida
options.C: The fallopian tube physically compresses the cells to keep them small
options.D: Cells divide so quickly that they shrink in mass with every cycle

explanation: Because the tough outer shell (zona pellucida) doesn't stretch right away, the dividing cells simply pack tighter into smaller spaces until they are ready to hatch.
