question: Why is giving plenty of fluids a top nursing priority during a sickle cell pain crisis?

options.A: It decreases blood viscosity, helping sickled cells flow through small vessels
options.B: It prevents the kidneys from filtering out necessary pain medications
options.C: It directly stops the bone marrow from producing abnormal haemoglobin S
options.D: It replaces the white blood cells that are lost during a hemolytic attack

explanation: Hydration is key! Fluids thin out the blood (reduces viscosity), making it much easier for those sticky cells to move through tight blood vessels.

question: When a patient is resting peacefully after a good meal, which part of their nervous system is hard at work?

options.A: Sympathetic division
options.B: Central integrative division
options.C: Parasympathetic division
options.D: Somatic motor division

explanation: Think 'rest and digest'! The parasympathetic system takes over when it's time to chill and recover energy. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h6)

question: What actually happens during a pelvic organ prolapse?

options.A: The descent of pelvic organs into or out of the vaginal canal
options.B: An infection of the lining of the uterus after childbirth
options.C: The complete closure of the vaginal opening due to scar tissue
options.D: A sudden spasm of the abdominal wall muscles

explanation: Great job! When the pelvic floor muscles get too weak, organs like the bladder or uterus can slip downward.

question: Besides keeping the skin clean, what is a key benefit of bathing a bedridden patient?

options.A: Preventing the patient from ever developing a fever
options.B: Completely eliminating the need for any pain medication
options.C: Stimulating blood circulation and assessing skin integrity
options.D: Lowering the patient's blood pressure permanently

explanation: Great job thinking clinically! Moving the skin and tissues gently during a bath boosts blood flow and gives you a wonderful chance to spot early signs of bedsores.

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care?

options.A: Improving the quality of life for patients and their families
options.B: Replacing all traditional medical treatments with herbal remedies
options.C: Accelerating the natural dying process through medication
options.D: Finding a permanent cure for terminal infectious diseases

explanation: Palliative care specifically aims to enhance quality of life by preventing and relieving suffering for both the patient and their loved ones during serious illness. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is a very common reason why patients stop taking their prescribed medications?

options.A: Doctors instruct them to hide their medications
options.B: Pharmacies always run out of standard packaging
options.C: They start feeling better and assume they are fully cured
options.D: They prefer keeping pills in their original boxes

explanation: Many individuals mistakenly believe that feeling better means the underlying illness has completely gone away. Patient education is key here!

question: What is the main way we define gender-based violence (GBV)?

options.A: Harmful acts based on sex or gender identity
options.B: Violent crimes committed exclusively against adult males
options.C: Accidental domestic injuries occurring at home
options.D: Physical injuries sustained during a street fight

explanation: GBV happens because of a person's sex or gender roles, rather than just random bad luck or street crime. You've got this!

question: What is the main goal of the Mother-Baby Package in healthcare?

options.A: To focus exclusively on emergency surgical procedures
options.B: To eliminate the need for community health extension workers
options.C: To provide essential health interventions for mothers and newborns together
options.D: To replace routine childhood immunization schedules

explanation: You got this! The Mother-Baby Package bundles care so that both mum and baby get the protection and support they need right from the start.

question: How does poor quality care directly impact women seeking reproductive health services?

options.A: It encourages them to report staff members to management
options.B: It forces them to demand more expensive medications
options.C: It drives them toward unsafe, alternative healthcare sources
options.D: It has no measurable effect on their health-seeking habits

explanation: Unwelcoming environments, rudeness, and poor treatment discourage clients from visiting formal facilities, pushing them to seek help elsewhere. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h1)

question: What structures divide the internal nasal cavity into left and right halves?

options.A: Nasal conchae
options.B: Nasal septum
options.C: Paranasal sinuses
options.D: Olfactory bulb

explanation: The nasal septum sits right down the middle, separating the left and right nasal cavities from each other. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h2)

question: Why must even experienced registered nurses take part in continuous professional development?

options.A: Experienced nurses tend to forget all basic nursing procedures
options.B: Medical knowledge and clinical techniques continuously evolve over time
options.C: Hospital accreditation boards punish facilities that do not hold daily exams
options.D: New nursing graduates require constant supervision from senior colleagues

explanation: Healthcare changes every day. Even senior nurses need continuous learning to stay sharp and master the newest, safest techniques. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h6)

question: Why must nurses carefully separate the concepts of sex and gender during patient assessments?

options.A: To change hospital administrative policies
options.B: To diagnose chromosomal disorders more cheaply
options.C: To avoid making false clinical assumptions about a patient based only on their anatomy
options.D: To ensure laboratory tests run faster

explanation: Brilliant! Knowing the difference stops us from stereotyping patients and helps us give safe, individualized care.

question: Why might some families prefer that health information be given to an elder rather than the patient?

options.A: The family is trying to hide insurance information from the hospital
options.B: Medical staff prefer speaking to older relatives over younger ones
options.C: The patient legally lacks the ability to understand any medical data
options.D: Cultural norms may dictate shared or family-centered decision-making

explanation: In many cultures, medical decisions are a collective family responsibility rather than an isolated individual choice. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h7)

question: A patient comes in with an incomplete abortion showing fever, lower belly pain, and foul-smelling discharge. What should you do first as the nurse?

options.A: Send the patient home with instructions to return next week
options.B: Administer high-dose fertility drugs to stimulate ovulation
options.C: Prepare for broad-spectrum antibiotics and report signs of infection
options.D: Withhold all fluids to prevent vomiting during the assessment

explanation: Spot on! Fever and foul discharge are classic warning signs of a septic abortion. Immediate antibiotics and medical stabilization are lifesavers here.

question: In drug supply and logistics, what does the term CIF stand for?

options.A: Cost, Insurance, and Freight
options.B: Client Invoice and Fee
options.C: Capital, Inventory, and Finance
options.D: Central Immunization Fund

explanation: CIF is just a handy shipping term! It covers the actual purchase price of imported drugs plus the cost of insurance and getting them safely delivered.

question: Which of these is checked as part of a standard biophysical profile (BPP) test?

options.A: Maternal blood pressure
options.B: Foetal blood gas values
options.C: Amniotic fluid volume
options.D: Placental hormone levels

explanation: Well done! A BPP uses ultrasound and monitoring to check five things: breathing, body movement, muscle tone, heart rate, and amniotic fluid volume. Keep up the fantastic work!

question: What does 'informed choice' truly mean in family planning counseling?

options.A: Clients must select the method with the highest efficacy rate.
options.B: Clients make voluntary decisions based on complete and accurate information.
options.C: Clients must follow the cultural preferences of their local community.
options.D: Nurses have the final authority to choose the method for the client.

explanation: Spot on! Informed choice means the client gets clear, unbiased facts so they can freely pick the method that works best for them without any pressure.

question: What symptom is most characteristic of gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD)?

options.A: Chronic constipation
options.B: Severe right shoulder pain
options.C: Heartburn
options.D: Projectile vomiting of blood

explanation: You've got it! Heartburn—that burning discomfort right behind your breastbone caused by acid irritation—is the classic hallmark of GORD.

question: What must you do if a labouring woman's progress on the partograph crosses over the action line?

options.A: Take immediate steps for intervention and management
options.B: Discharge the patient home for rest
options.C: Wait another four hours without changes
options.D: Switch from monitoring vitals to once daily

explanation: Spot on! Crossing the action line is a clear warning sign that labour isn't going as smoothly as expected, so prompt medical action is required to help mother and baby.

question: A patient with an advanced illness is physically stable, but their family looks completely exhausted and anxious. What should you do as the nurse?

options.A: Ask the doctor to discharge the patient immediately to relieve stress
options.B: Tell the family to go home and rest until the patient's condition worsens
options.C: Focus only on the patient since their physical vitals are stable
options.D: Include the family's coping capacity as part of your ongoing assessment

explanation: When the family is worn out, it affects the patient too! Checking in on how the family is coping is a vital part of good nursing care.

question: How do deep, slow breathing exercises physically help a patient calm down?

options.A: They increase skeletal muscle tension to release trapped toxins
options.B: They permanently block the adrenal glands from producing cortisol
options.C: They flood the bloodstream with extra adrenaline to burn off energy
options.D: They stimulate the vagus nerve to activate the parasympathetic nervous system

explanation: Deep breathing acts like a brake pedal for your nervous system, stimulating the vagus nerve to switch you from 'fight-or-flight' to 'rest-and-digest.' [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h7)

question: As a night nurse, what is the best way to help reduce environmental stress for patients on a busy ward?

options.A: Leave the overhead fluorescent lights on so staff can monitor safely
options.B: Turn up the monitor alarm volumes so they can be heard down the hall
options.C: Cluster nursing care activities to allow longer periods of uninterrupted sleep
options.D: Encourage visitors to stay past visiting hours to keep spirits high

explanation: By grouping your tasks together (like doing vitals and giving meds at the same time), you let patients sleep peacefully without waking them up every hour. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h7)

question: What is a practical way for a hospital to handle language barriers with patients?

options.A: Using written English pamphlets exclusively for all health education
options.B: Refusing admission to anyone who does not speak the official language
options.C: Providing translation services or multilingual staff members
options.D: Requiring all patients to learn medical terminology before booking an appointment

explanation: Spot on! Having translators or staff who speak local languages helps patients fully understand their care.

question: What is the main goal of doing a Spontaneous Breathing Trial (SBT)?

options.A: To measure the exact lung compliance and resistance parameters
options.B: To evaluate if a patient can tolerate breathing without ventilator support
options.C: To allow the patient to recover from heavy sedative medications
options.D: To clear thick mucus plugs from the lower airways before extubation

explanation: An SBT is like a test drive! We lower the machine's help to see if the patient's lungs and muscles are strong enough to handle breathing all on their own.

question: Why do patients with untreated diabetes sometimes experience rapid weight loss?

options.A: Excessive fluid intake flushes away all dietary nutrients
options.B: High blood sugar levels speed up the normal metabolic rate
options.C: Kidneys filter out solid food particles into the urine
options.D: The body breaks down stored fat and muscle for energy

explanation: When glucose can't enter the cells for fuel, the body panics and starts burning its own fat and muscle instead, causing sudden weight loss. Makes total sense when you picture it!

question: Why is clear, informed consent so important before a couple starts IVF treatment?

options.A: Because nurses are legally required to adopt any resulting children
options.B: Because it prevents patients from ever experiencing natural conception again
options.C: Because decisions must be made early about storing or donating leftover embryos
options.D: Because IVF is completely illegal under all Nigerian federal statutes

explanation: Since IVF creates extra embryos, couples must agree in advance on what will happen to them to avoid future legal and emotional conflicts. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h6)

question: A patient's joint fluid report mentions hemarthrosis. What does this mean?

options.A: Normal wear and tear from aging
options.B: A severe bacterial infection in the joint
options.C: An advanced stage of rheumatoid arthritis
options.D: Recent trauma or bleeding inside the joint

explanation: Hemarthrosis simply means there is blood inside the joint space. You will usually see this after a physical injury, a heavy fall, or recent joint surgery.

question: In ventilator settings, what does the term PEEP stand for?

options.A: Positive end-expiratory pressure
options.B: Primary external air pressure
options.C: Peak elastic expiration pressure
options.D: Pulmonary evaluation and expansion protocol

explanation: PEEP leaves a tiny bit of pressure in the lungs right at the end of a breath. This stops the tiny air sacs from collapsing like deflated balloons!

question: Why should nurses care about why patients stay silent when safety rules are skipped?

options.A: It reduces the need to sterilize reusable equipment
options.B: Patients are usually at fault for bad clinical outcomes
options.C: It proves that hospitals have enough medical supplies
options.D: Understanding patient silence helps nurses improve safety advocacy

explanation: You got it! When we understand why patients keep quiet, we can break those barriers and speak up better for their safety.

question: A student appears unusually quiet, withdraws from peers, and drops in academic performance. What does this situation call for?

options.A: Assessment for potential mental well-being concerns
options.B: Immediate suspension for classroom disruption
options.C: Mandatory physical exercise drills after hours
options.D: Restriction from all school feeding programmes

explanation: Sudden behavioral and academic changes are classic red flags for underlying mental or emotional stress in students. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h3)

question: You are reviving a woman with severe shock from bleeding. What size of IV cannula should you secure first?

options.A: 22-gauge green cannula
options.B: 24-gauge yellow cannula
options.C: 16-gauge or 18-gauge large-bore cannula
options.D: 26-gauge tiny pediatric cannula

explanation: You got it! Large-bore cannulas let fluids and blood flow in rapidly when treating severe shock. In an emergency, bigger is definitely better!

question: A nurse finishes dressing a wound soaked with infected pus. Where should the soiled gauze dressing be discarded?

options.A: Cardboard medication box
options.B: General recycling container
options.C: Yellow infectious waste bag
options.D: Black domestic waste bin

explanation: Infectious clinical waste containing body fluids goes into the yellow bag to prevent the spread of pathogens. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of physiotherapy in long-term MS care?

options.A: Maintaining mobility and preventing joint stiffness
options.B: Analyzing cerebrospinal fluid laboratory samples
options.C: Performing surgical repair of demyelinated nerves
options.D: Prescribing disease-modifying drug dosages

explanation: Physiotherapy keeps muscles working, improves balance, and prevents tight joints (contractures), helping the patient stay active for as long as possible.

question: Why is opening the airway the top priority in emergency care?

options.A: It prevents patients from talking too loudly
options.B: Blocked air passages quickly lead to brain death
options.C: It stops internal bone bleeding immediately
options.D: Doctors cannot write prescriptions without it

explanation: Without a clear airway, oxygen cannot reach the brain. Brain cells start dying in minutes without oxygen, so we must clear the airway first!

question: A nurse is checking the chart before giving IV ondansetron. Which pre-existing heart condition means you need to be extra careful?

options.A: History of peptic ulcers
options.B: Prolonged QT interval
options.C: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Mild essential hypertension

explanation: Spot on! 5-HT3 drugs can affect heart electrical rhythms, so a patient with a long QT interval is at risk for serious heart rhythm issues. Safety first in nursing!

question: Why must a home care plan be flexible rather than completely rigid?

options.A: So the nurse can visit whenever it is convenient for them
options.B: To bypass the need for approval from the primary physician
options.C: To fit smoothly into the patient's personal daily routines
options.D: Because insurance companies change policies every single week

explanation: If a care plan respects and fits into a patient's normal daily habits, they are much more likely to follow it successfully. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h3)

question: A patient gets a painkiller derived from the opium poppy after surgery. Which drug is it?

options.A: Quinine
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Morphine
options.D: Digoxin

explanation: Morphine is a powerful pain-relieving medication extracted right from the opium poppy plant. You'll see this often in clinicals!

question: Which complication frequently develops following prolonged low blood pressure and shock from severe bleeding?

options.A: Acute kidney injury
options.B: Enlargement of the spleen
options.C: Excessive bone mineralization
options.D: Chronic high blood pressure

explanation: When blood flow drops significantly during shock, the kidneys suffer from oxygen deprivation, which can lead to acute kidney damage. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h7)

question: How many blood vessels are normally inside a healthy human umbilical cord?

options.A: Two arteries and two veins
options.B: Two veins and one artery
options.C: Two arteries and one vein
options.D: One artery and one vein

explanation: Correct! A normal umbilical cord has three vessels: two umbilical arteries carrying waste away from the baby, and one umbilical vein bringing fresh oxygen and nutrients. Easy peasy!

question: Which brain chemical is most closely linked to the reward system and feelings of pleasure?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Histamine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Great job! Dopamine is the brain's main messenger for making us feel good and reinforcing rewarding behaviors. Think of it as the brain's natural 'feel-good' chemical.

question: Why do nurses play such a big role in carrying out the Essential Drug Programme?

options.A: They work exclusively inside administrative pharmacy offices
options.B: They control the international import budgets for pharmaceuticals
options.C: They interact with patients daily and manage bedside drug use
options.D: They are legally licensed to manufacture commercial vaccines

explanation: Spot on! As a nurse, you are right on the frontline—giving medications, tracking supplies, and teaching patients every single day.

question: Which blood test is more specific for diagnosing acute pancreatitis?

options.A: Hemoglobin
options.B: Lipase
options.C: Creatinine
options.D: Albumin

explanation: Spot on! Serum lipase is the go-to test because it's much more specific to the pancreas than amylase, and it stays elevated longer during an attack.

question: Which home modification is most helpful for preventing bathroom falls?

options.A: Placing soft throw rugs on the tile floor
options.B: Installing grab bars and non-slip mats
options.C: Using dim lighting to avoid harsh glares
options.D: Keeping the bathroom door locked at night

explanation: Wet bathroom surfaces are extremely slick, making grab bars and non-slip mats essential safety additions. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h3)

question: When starting an eye irrigation, where do you aim the stream of fluid?

options.A: Directly onto the center of the black pupil
options.B: At the outer corner, flowing inward toward the nose
options.C: Directly against the upper eyelid skin
options.D: At the inner canthus, flowing toward the outer canthus

explanation: Always flow from the inside corner (near the nose) toward the outside corner. This follows natural tear flow and keeps junk out of the tear ducts!

question: What do we mean by 'patient harm' in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Injury caused by medical care rather than the underlying disease
options.B: Emotional distress caused by a patient's personal family issues
options.C: Discomfort experienced before a formal diagnosis is made
options.D: Natural progression of a chronic illness over time

explanation: Spot on! Patient harm refers specifically to injuries that happen because of the medical care or treatment provided, rather than the natural course of the sickness itself. Keep up the great thinking!

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge facing DRF exemptions in public hospitals?

options.A: Persistent stockouts caused by lack of reimbursement
options.B: Bureaucratic delays in patient verification
options.C: Exploitation of loopholes by non-indigent individuals
options.D: Excessive government funding that overflows the pharmacy

explanation: If only! Public hospitals rarely have excessive funding; instead, they constantly battle underfunding and delayed subventions.

question: Why is it helpful to encourage small, manageable daily goals for a patient struggling with severe depression?

options.A: It prevents the patient from feeling overwhelmed by large tasks
options.B: It eliminates the need for any prescribed medication
options.C: It guarantees the patient will return to work immediately
options.D: It cures the chemical imbalance in the brain instantly

explanation: You got it! Depression drains energy. Breaking the day into tiny, doable steps helps patients feel a sense of success without crashing from exhaustion.

question: What triggers a secondary oocyte to finish its second meiotic division?

options.A: The successful entry and fusion of a sperm cell
options.B: The complete shedding of the endometrial lining
options.C: A sudden drop in systemic progesterone levels
options.D: The physical passage of the egg through the cervix

explanation: The egg stays paused in its development process until a sperm successfully enters, giving it the green light to finish dividing.

question: What is the job of transferrin in the body?

options.A: It filters water-soluble vitamins out of the blood for renal excretion.
options.B: It acts as a transport protein that carries iron through the bloodstream.
options.C: It stores excess calcium inside the dense matrix of long bones.
options.D: It produces active vitamin D inside the cells of the renal cortex.

explanation: Think of transferrin as a dedicated taxi in your blood plasma. Its sole job is to pick up iron and safely drive it to places like your bone marrow!

question: What is the most common mild side effect patients report when taking oral expectorants?

options.A: Nausea and gastrointestinal upset
options.B: Sudden loss of color vision
options.C: Permanent hearing loss in both ears
options.D: Severe high blood pressure spikes

explanation: Spot on. Because these drugs work by slightly irritating the stomach lining, mild tummy upset or nausea can sometimes happen.

question: What is a major risk or downside if team leadership on the ward is weak?

options.A: Patients refusing to take any hospital medications
options.B: Automatic promotion of all junior staff members
options.C: Blurred responsibilities and fragmented patient care
options.D: Doctors taking over all nursing responsibilities

explanation: That's right! When leadership lacks clear direction, team members get confused about who is supposed to do what, leading to gaps in patient care.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical sign of joint inflammation that nurses look for?

options.A: Pain when moving the affected limb
options.B: Stiffness, especially after resting
options.C: Normal skin color and cool temperature
options.D: Swelling around the joint area

explanation: Spot on! Inflamed joints are usually warm, red, swollen, and painful—not cool and normal-looking!

question: What happens right away to the tissue when teeth pierce the skin?

options.A: The body instantly creates a permanent protective scar barrier
options.B: The immune system seals the puncture wound with sterile fluid
options.C: All surrounding blood vessels dilate to neutralize the foreign saliva
options.D: Oral bacteria are pushed directly into sterile tissue planes

explanation: The sheer mechanical action of a bite breaks the skin barrier and inoculates mouth germs straight into the vulnerable underlying tissue.

question: Why is stomach pumping (gastric lavage) rarely done if a patient seeks help hours after swallowing a poison?

options.A: Gastric lavage only works on poisons that were inhaled
options.B: The poison has already passed from the stomach into the small intestines
options.C: Activated charcoal neutralizes the need for any washing
options.D: The stomach lining becomes too tough for tubes to pass safely

explanation: Makes total sense, right? If hours have passed, the poison has already moved past the stomach, making pumping ineffective.

question: During which weeks of pregnancy is a baby most at risk for birth defects from harmful drugs?

options.A: The first two weeks following conception
options.B: The final two weeks before anticipated birth
options.C: Weeks three through eight of the first trimester
options.D: Throughout the entire third trimester

explanation: This is the major window when little organs are actively forming (organogenesis), making weeks 3 to 8 the most sensitive time.

question: What is the most important thing to check on a mother right after she delivers?

options.A: Visual acuity and hearing reflex responses
options.B: Uterine tone and amount of vaginal bleeding
options.C: Serum electrolyte levels and kidney function
options.D: Bowel motility and digestive enzyme output

explanation: Safety first! Checking that the uterus feels firm and watching the bleeding amount helps you catch heavy postpartum bleeding early.

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard component of post-haemorrhage nursing care?

options.A: Restricting all movement for at least two weeks
options.B: Watching for signs of surgical site infection
options.C: Assessing the patient for anxiety and fear
options.D: Monitoring haemoglobin and haematocrit blood levels

explanation: Total immobility is harmful and increases the risk of blood clots; early mobilization is encouraged as soon as the patient is stable. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h7)

question: Where is milk actually manufactured inside the breast?

options.A: Nipple pores
options.B: Adipose cells
options.C: Areola glands
options.D: Alveoli

explanation: Alveoli are tiny, hollow sacs lined with milk-secreting cells where lactation actually takes place. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h4)

question: What makes an IV fluid 'isotonic'?

options.A: It draws fluid out of the blood vessels and into the tissue cells
options.B: It contains large protein molecules that cannot cross membranes
options.C: It causes body cells to swell by forcing water inside them
options.D: It has the same particle concentration as blood plasma

explanation: You've got this! Isotonic fluids match the natural concentration of our blood, meaning they safely boost fluid volume without causing water to rush into or out of our cells.

question: A male patient appears quiet and defensive during his fertility workup. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Reassure him that male infertility is always easily cured with surgery
options.B: Provide a private, non-judgmental environment to discuss his concerns openly
options.C: Refer him immediately to a psychiatrist for severe clinical depression
options.D: Insist that his wife answers all the clinical questions for him

explanation: Creating a safe, supportive space helps lower defenses and encourages the patient to share his emotional burdens. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h8)

question: Which part of the male urethra is the widest and passes straight through the prostate gland?

options.A: Preprostatic segment
options.B: Spongy segment
options.C: Prostatic segment
options.D: Membranous segment

explanation: Well done! The prostatic urethra gets its name because it is snugly encased by the prostate gland.

question: What is the main purpose of a preceptorship program for new nurses?

options.A: To make them work double shifts without extra pay
options.B: To test their memory with surprise written examinations
options.C: To pair them with an experienced nurse for guidance and support
options.D: To teach them how to manage hospital finances

explanation: Preceptors guide new staff through real clinical situations, helping them gain confidence and adjust smoothly. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h4)

question: Which viral infection is strongly linked to causing cervical cancer in women?

options.A: Human immunodeficiency virus
options.B: Human papillomavirus
options.C: Epstein-Barr virus
options.D: Hepatitis B virus

explanation: High-risk strains of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) can cause cellular changes over time, which is why screening and vaccines are so important.

question: What part of the fibrous tunic is completely clear to let light pass into the eye?

options.A: Cornea
options.B: Retina
options.C: Sclera
options.D: Choroid

explanation: The cornea is the transparent front window of the eye that bends and admits light. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the top nursing priority right after major cancer surgery?

options.A: Withdrawing all intravenous fluids immediately
options.B: Preventing complications and managing acute surgical pain
options.C: Discharging the patient within twenty-four hours
options.D: Starting intensive physical exercise right away

explanation: Right after surgery, keeping your patient comfortable and watching out for issues like infection or blood clots are your most important duties. You are well on your way to becoming an amazing nurse!

question: A patient develops sudden severe shortness of breath, restlessness, and absent breath sounds on the treated side after a thoracocentesis. What is the nurse's priority action?

options.A: Administer a mild oral pain medication and check vital signs in one hour
options.B: Remove the dressing and apply warm compresses to the puncture site
options.C: Encourage the patient to take slow, deep breaths to clear the airways
options.D: Notify the provider immediately and prepare for a chest tube insertion

explanation: Absent breath sounds and severe shortness of breath point to a significant pneumothorax or lung collapse, which is a medical emergency. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h7)

question: Which brain structure forms the roof at the back of the fourth ventricle?

options.A: Pituitary gland
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Frontal cortex
options.D: Olfactory bulb

explanation: Correct! The fourth ventricle sits right in front of the cerebellum, which forms its lovely protective roof at the back.

question: What is the nurse's main job when assessing a patient's diet?

options.A: Designing commercial meal delivery services
options.B: Prescribing strict hospital therapeutic diets
options.C: Collecting and evaluating food intake data
options.D: Purchasing nutritional supplements for wards

explanation: You've got this! Nurses gather information on what patients eat to spot any nutrition risks early and plan the best care possible.

question: Which factor can cause a false-negative Mantoux result in someone who actually has TB?

options.A: Receiving a fresh dose of the PPD antigen
options.B: Reading the test exactly at 48 hours
options.C: Severe immunosuppression from advanced HIV
options.D: Having a history of latent tuberculosis infection

explanation: If the immune system is deeply suppressed, it might not put up any fight at all, leaving you with a blank (false-negative) skin test even if TB is present. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h7)

question: A young adult with sickle cell disease is preparing for a mountain hiking trip. What is the most important warning the nurse should give?

options.A: Cold mountain water will permanently cure chronic joint inflammation
options.B: Low oxygen levels at high altitudes can trigger a painful sickling crisis
options.C: Hiking boots will cause severe foot ulcers due to poor circulation
options.D: Mountain air contains too many allergens that destroy red blood cells

explanation: High altitudes have lower oxygen levels, which can easily provoke red blood cells to change shape and block blood flow. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h5)

question: What is the best lab sample to take when checking for a polio infection?

options.A: Sputum sample
options.B: Blood culture
options.C: Urine sample
options.D: Stool sample

explanation: You nailed it! Since the virus multiplies happily in the gut, stool samples are the most reliable way for the lab to find it.

question: When a community nurse teaches local mothers about healthy weaning foods for babies, what role is she playing?

options.A: Pharmacist
options.B: Hospital administrator
options.C: Surgeon
options.D: Educator

explanation: Well done! Sharing helpful health tips and teaching families makes you a wonderful health educator.

question: What is the main reason a nurse gives a beta-blocker to someone with hyperthyroidism?

options.A: Controlling rapid heart rate, tremors, and anxiety symptoms
options.B: Replacing depleted stores of thyroxine in peripheral tissues
options.C: Permanently destroying hyperactive thyroid cells with radiation
options.D: Stopping the thyroid gland from synthesizing new hormones

explanation: Beta-blockers act like a calming shield, quickly easing that racing heart, shaking, and jittery feeling while other meds kick in.

question: Which of the following is a common sign of chronic poor systemic circulation in the lower extremities?

options.A: Excessive sweating on the soles of feet
options.B: Sudden swelling with a hot red surface
options.C: Slow-healing sores or ulcers on the feet
options.D: Inability to move the toes at all

explanation: Poor blood flow means tissues lack the nutrients and oxygen needed to repair minor cuts, leading to slow-healing wounds. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h8)

question: Why should a nurse check lab results before encouraging a patient to take high-dose supplements?

options.A: To find out if the patient is allergic to plastic medicine bottles
options.B: To make sure the patient can afford the expensive brand names sold in pharmacies
options.C: To calculate the exact hospital bed tax for nutritional therapy
options.D: To confirm the specific nutrient deficiency rather than guessing based on general fatigue

explanation: We test to be sure what's actually lacking. Guessing can lead to wasting money or even vitamin toxicity!

question: Why is eating or drinking inside a chemical storage room a major safety violation?

options.A: It creates a direct pathway for hand-to-mouth chemical ingestion
options.B: It attracts pests that chew through the chemical packaging
options.C: Digestion slows down significantly in cold storage rooms
options.D: Food particles will ruin the chemical composition of stored products

explanation: Exactly right! Invisible chemical residues can settle on your hands, food, or drinks, making it super easy to swallow them by accident. Always keep food and drinks well away from chemicals!

question: Why do we often use a mix of different therapies to manage chronic pain in patients with physical disabilities?

options.A: Single medications are completely ineffective for all types of nerve pain
options.B: Non-pharmacological methods remove the need for any clinical supervision
options.C: Combining different therapies addresses multiple underlying causes of pain safely
options.D: Pain associated with physical disabilities always resolves spontaneously

explanation: Chronic pain has many layers, so combining meds and physical therapy gives better relief without needing dangerously high drug doses. Smart approach!

question: What is a major systemic challenge frequently facing primary health care centers in Nigeria today?

options.A: Too many operational hospitals with zero patients
options.B: Excessive supplies of clean water and electricity
options.C: An overwhelming surplus of highly paid medical doctors in every village
options.D: Chronic underfunding and shortages of essential drugs

explanation: Correct. Sadly, many primary health centers struggle with basic funding, poor infrastructure, and running out of essential medicines.

question: What main change happens inside an artery during atherosclerosis?

options.A: Capillaries multiply rapidly to bypass the area
options.B: Valves inside the artery begin to leak blood
options.C: Smooth muscle in the wall permanently stretches out
options.D: Fatty plaques build up and narrow the inside of the vessel

explanation: Think of atherosclerosis like rust building up inside a pipe. Fats and fibrous tissue collect inside the artery wall, making the pathway narrower for blood flow.

question: How does Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) primarily help someone deal with anxiety?

options.A: By prescribing strong sedative medications for daily use
options.B: By using physical exercise to tire out the nervous system
options.C: By teaching the patient how to avoid all stressful life events
options.D: By replacing negative or distorted thoughts with realistic ones

explanation: CBT is all about catching those sneaky, unhelpful thought patterns and learning how to flip them into grounded, balanced perspectives.

question: Which key community figures can nurses partner with to encourage male involvement?

options.A: Commercial vehicle drivers
options.B: Secondary school prefects
options.C: Traditional rulers and religious leaders
options.D: International airline pilots

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders command great respect and can easily help shift community attitudes toward male participation.

question: A village school lacks a clean water supply, putting children at risk of waterborne diseases. What is the best community-driven action to take?

options.A: Wait until the national government builds a modern university teaching hospital
options.B: Advise all students to stop drinking water while inside the school premises
options.C: Mobilize local leaders and artisans to sink a borehole or repair water tanks
options.D: Close down the school permanently until international aid arrives

explanation: Local mobilization utilizes community labor and donations to solve immediate health infrastructure challenges practically. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T6#GNS225_U4_T6_h3)

question: After a safe delivery, which eye ointment do you apply right away to protect a newborn from eye infections?

options.A: Atropine sulfate drops
options.B: Chloramphenicol eye drops
options.C: Hydrocortisone eye gel
options.D: Tetracycline eye ointment

explanation: Brilliant! Tetracycline 1% eye ointment is standard care to shield baby's eyes from harmful bacteria passed during birth.

question: A study shows that patients with higher anxiety report higher pain levels. Why can the researcher NOT claim that anxiety causes the pain?

options.A: Because anxiety is an experimental variable
options.B: Because pain cannot be measured using numerical scales
options.C: Because the sample size was likely too small to matter
options.D: Because correlational designs do not test cause and effect

explanation: Spot on! Finding a connection between two things just shows they move together; it doesn't prove one actually caused the other. Correlation is not causation!

question: What kind of muscle weakness or paralysis is typical in polio?

options.A: Flaccid paralysis
options.B: Decerebrate paralysis
options.C: Rigid paralysis
options.D: Spastic paralysis

explanation: Spot on! When lower motor neurons are destroyed, the muscles lose their tone and become limp and floppy—this is known as flaccid paralysis.

question: A patient just returned to the ward after a cerebral angiogram through the groin. What is a key nursing duty?

options.A: Checking the puncture site for bleeding and checking pulses below it
options.B: Restricting all drinking water for 24 hours
options.C: Removing the pressure bandage within the first ten minutes
options.D: Telling the patient to get up and walk around immediately

explanation: Always keep an eye on the puncture site and check the foot pulse to catch any bleeding or clotting early!

question: What primary problem led to the invention of the Coronary Care Unit (CCU)?

options.A: High rates of severe bleeding during routine blood pressure checks
options.B: Sudden, unrecognized lethal heart rhythms causing unexpected cardiac arrests
options.C: A massive shortage of beds for patients suffering from severe pneumonia
options.D: The frequent occurrence of surgical wound infections after heart operations

explanation: CCUs were created to continuously monitor heart patients so dangerous rhythms could be treated immediately before the heart stopped. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h4)
